### `discussionboard_sections`

Board Section entity - This implements the requirement for organizing multiple boards into logical sections/category headings as described in the requirements (see Business Overview and Board API). 

Provides top-level grouping for boards (e.g., 'Politics', 'Economy'). Each section contains multiple boards but supports explicit sorting and labeling for easy discovery. Maintains 3NF by storing only section-specific data and referencing boards elsewhere. 

Example: Used for filtering the board list UI, and configuring board display order in admin settings.
Key relationships: One section to many boards (referenced from discussionboard_boards). 
Special behaviors: Deletions should be restricted if boards exist within a section.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a section.
- `name`: Section name - Implements the section/categorization requirement. Human-readable name to display to users (e.g., 'Politics'). 3NF maintained by storing only the atomic label here. Example: Section dropdown in UI.
- `description`: Section description - Short text clarifying purpose or scope. 3NF compliant atomic text. Example: 'For regional and national issues.'
- `sort_order`: Explicit sort order for UI display - Allows admin-defined ordering of sections. Maintains 3NF by only storing atomic order number. Example: Integer used for section sorting.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Implements audit and data retention requirement. 3NF as an atomic date-time value. Example: used for sorting/recently added filter.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp - Used for audits and last-modified displays. Example: UI 'last updated' column.

### `discussionboard_boards`

Board entity - Implements the requirement for multiple thematic boards within the platform (see Business Overview, API spec). 

Represents a specific discussion board (e.g., 'Elections 2025'). Each board belongs to a section and can have subscriptions, tags, settings, etc. Maintains 3NF by separating board details from posts/content, and referencing only the relevant section. 

Example: Used for displaying board list, posting endpoints, and enforcing board-level settings.
Key relationships: Many-to-one with discussionboard_sections (foreign key); referenced by other tables for posts, subscriptions, and tags.
Special behaviors: Section deletion/renaming cascades/updates needed; cannot delete section if boards exist.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a board.
- `discussionboard_section_id`: Belonged section's [discussionboard_sections.id](#discussionboard_sections) - Links board to its section for groupings. Required to ensure boards are organized. Maintains referential integrity and 3NF.
- `name`: Board name - Implements the logical board separation requirement. Human-readable board title (e.g., 'Elections 2025'). Strictly atomic per 3NF. Example: Board selector UI.
- `description`: Board description - Explanatory text for users to understand board's focus. Enforces 3NF by storing only description here. Example: Board hover tooltip.
- `rules`: Custom board-specific rules (markdown/plaintext) - Implements requirement for community rules per board. Maintains 3NF. Example: Board custom code of conduct.
- `is_active`: Active/inactive flag - Used by admins to hide inactive/archived boards. Follows 3NF by being an atomic status indicator. Example: Board visibility toggle.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the board - For audits, logs, and recency filters. 3NF atomic timestamp. Example: Used in new board creation tracking.
- `updated_at`: Last updated time - For audit trail and change tracking. Example: UI listing.

### `discussionboard_tags`

Tag entity - Implements the requirement for tagging boards and enabling filtered search/discovery (see Functional Requirements and API spec). 

Stores tag definitions for use on boards or posts. Tags can be assigned to boards (via M:N relationship implemented in other domain if needed). Maintains 3NF as a definition-only table; actual assignments are managed elsewhere. 

Example: Used for board tag suggestions, filtering board/post lists. 
Key relationships: Used in tag-board mappings but maintains strict normalization here.
Special behaviors: Only atomic data stored; all application-side assignment linked elsewhere.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique tag identifier.
- `tag`: Tag value - Human-friendly tag (e.g., 'policy', 'economy'). Implements tag definition requirement. Enforces normalization by keeping atomic labels only here. Example: Tag chips in UI.
- `description`: Tag description - Explains scope/purpose of tag for admin and users. Enforces 3NF. Example: Tag hover info.
- `created_at`: Tag creation timestamp - Required for record keeping. Maintains 3NF. Example: Used for sorting tags by newest.
- `updated_at`: Last tag update time - For audit logs and change history in admin UI. 3NF compliant.

### `discussionboard_board_subscriptions`

Board subscription entity - Implements the board subscription/notification feature (see Notification System and Functional Requirements). 

Tracks which members are subscribed to which boards, to drive notifications and update feeds. Maintains 3NF as a pure M:N/junction entity: each record (subscription) is atomic, linking a single user to a single board. 

Example: Used for fast lookup of a member's subscribed boards, or when sending board notifications. 
Key relationships: Foreign keys to boards (this file) and discussionboard_members (external Actors component). 
Special behaviors: Unsubscribe (soft delete or remove record); composite uniqueness enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique subscription ID.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Subscribed board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards) - Enforces which board is subscribed. Enforces 3NF as atomic foreign key. Example: All subscriptions for a board.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Subscribed member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) (from Actors component) - Links subscription to member (ALREADY CREATED in Actors schema). 3NF: purely as a foreign key. Example: All user subscriptions.
- `created_at`: Time of subscription - For audit/logging, 3NF as single timestamp. Example: Recent subscriber statistics.

### `discussionboard_board_settings`

Board settings entity - Implements requirement for customizable settings per board (see Functional Requirements and Board API). 

Stores various administrative or feature settings per board (e.g., allow images, require moderator approval). Maintains 3NF: atomic settings per board, without computed fields; extensible. 

Example: Used to toggle features for specific boards or override defaults.
Key relationships: Unique per board (1:1 with boards). 
Special behaviors: Board can have only one settings record; model extensible for future settings.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for board settings.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Target board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards) - Settings apply to this board. Enforced unique for 1:1. Example: Feature toggle lookup for a specific board.
- `allow_images`: Allow image uploads - Implements toggle for image posting. 3NF: atomic flag only, actual images handled elsewhere. Example: Image post permissions UI.
- `require_moderator_approval`: Require moderator approval for new posts - Supports moderation flow requirement. 3NF flag only. Example: Restricted board setup.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for audit/history. 3NF as atomic timestamp. Example: For admin settings log.
- `updated_at`: Last updated time for settings, for auditing. Example: Settings history tracking.

### `discussionboard_notification_settings`

User notification setting entity - Implements user preference storage for receiving board/content notifications (see Notification System and Functional Requirements). 

Stores per-user notification toggles/preferences for the Discussion Board domain. Maintains 3NF by keeping atomic preference values per user. Used to configure which types of notifications are received (thread activity, announcements, etc). 

Example: Used when sending notification emails, or rendering notification settings UI. 
Key relationships: Linked to members (via discussionboard_member_id from Actors component).
Special behaviors: Unique-per-user enforced, 1:1 with member record.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique notification setting ID.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) (from Actors component) - Which member these preferences apply to. Unique for 1:1. Example: Editing notification preferences for logged-in member.
- `receive_board_notifications`: Receive notifications for new board activity/posts - Implements the core notification toggle. 3NF as atomic preference. Example: User settings UI toggle.
- `receive_mention_notifications`: Receive mention notifications - Controls alerts for mentions/replies. 3NF flag. Example: Mention alert switch on settings page.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for notification prefs history/audit. 3NF.
- `updated_at`: Last prefs update timestamp, for audit/history. 3NF.

### `discussionboard_admins`

Platform administrator role assignment - Implements the functional requirement for privileged admin accounts as found in the requirements (see: User Roles & Permissions). 

Administrators oversee content and user moderation at the highest level; this table records accounts with full platform control and is central for RBAC enforcement. Maintains strict 3NF normalization by storing only direct attributes of the admin role, referencing user membership via foreign key. For example, promotes a member to admin role or demotes. 

Key relationships: links to discussionboard_members (user basis), may be referenced in audit logs or moderation actions.  Special behaviors: Granting this role cascades full access; must be auditable.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique admin role record identifier.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Assigns admin privileges to a registered member.
- `granted_at`: Datetime when admin role was granted. Implements temporal auditability as per action trail requirements. For example, captures promotion time.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime when admin role was revoked (if applicable). Null unless admin privileges are removed. Supports audit and compliance.

### `discussionboard_moderators`

Moderator role assignment - Implements the requirement for a moderation role to enforce community guidelines (see: Moderation Roles & Policies, Permissions Matrix).

This table records which members serve as moderators. It maintains strict normalization by referencing user membership while tracking assignment and revocation dates. Used for permission elevation, logging, and audit trails. For example, a user promoted from member to moderator.

Key relationships: References discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: Can be demoted; actions logged for accountability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique moderator assignment record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - the member elevated to moderator role.
- `granted_at`: Datetime when moderator role was granted. Implements temporal audit trail for promotions. For example, captures elevation to moderator.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime when moderator role was revoked (null if active). Supports demotion/historical queries.

### `discussionboard_members`

Registered discussion board user accounts (members) - Implements registration/authentication requirements (User Authentication & Roles, CRUD Permissions).

This table represents all registered, authenticated users. It enforces 3NF by storing only per-user, non-derived data. For example, account creation, activation status, ban integration and role assignment references.

Key relationships: Referenced by admin, moderator, profile, and user email tables. Special behaviors: Used for primary ownership of posts/comments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique member account identifier.
- `username`: Account username - unique member login handle fulfilling the registration requirement; not case-sensitive and normalized for identity mapping. Ensures user uniqueness at platform level. Example: johndoe.
- `password_hash`: Hashed password for secure authentication (never raw password), per non-functional security requirement. Complies with encryption policy and data protection. Example: bcrypt or Argon2 hash string.
- `created_at`: Datetime when member account was created. Implements registration audit trail and supports search/sorting. Example: upon sign up.
- `activated_at`: Datetime when account was activated/completed verification. Null if not verified yet. Example: after email confirmation workflow.
- `deactivated_at`: Datetime of account deactivation (soft delete or permanent). Null if active. Supports retention policy and reactivation scenarios.

### `discussionboard_guests`

Guest user visitation - Implements guest journey tracking for unauthenticated users (see: User Roles & Journeys, Audit Trail).

This table stores guest/browser sessions for analytics, restrictions, and future up-sell. Maintains normalized structure by storing atomic session info only, not mixing with registered user data. For example, may log guest page views or promote registration.

Key relationships: May later link to discussionboard_members if guest converts to member.
Special behaviors: Short-lived; can be joined to logs for traffic analysis.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique guest session identifier.
- `session_token`: Opaque session cookie or token identifying the guest browser. Supports uniqueness and privacy tracking. For example: UUID or secure random token.
- `created_at`: Datetime guest session was initiated. Implements guest activity timeline; supports reporting and session expiry logic.

### `discussionboard_user_profiles`

Extended member profile details - Implements profile customization as per member/user journey requirements.

This table holds profile metadata (bio, display name, avatar, etc.), referencing the core member account. Maintains normalization by separating profile from core authentication/role. Example: user changes display name or avatar; updates here without affecting core login.

Key relationships: Foreign key to discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: all fields except member linkage are nullable, allowing partial profiles.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique profile record identifier.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). One-to-one mapping from member to user profile.
- `display_name`: Public display name or nickname for the user (not required to match username). Implements customization requirement as per usability guideline. Example: John R.
- `bio`: Short user biography or introduction, as per personalization feature. Maintains normalized structure; null if not set.
- `avatar_url`: Profile image/avatar URI, facilitating multimedia enhancement and personalization. Null if not provided; stored as URI string. Example: https://cdn.site/avatar/123.
- `created_at`: Datetime profile was created. Implements audit trail for customization events.
- `updated_at`: Datetime profile was last updated, supports version awareness for profile changes. Enables profile history tracking.

### `discussionboard_user_emails`

Email addresses associated with member accounts - Implements requirements for registration, verification, contact and notification preferences (Functional: Registration & Email Verification).

Maintains one-to-many normalized mapping for supporting multiple verified emails per account, anti-abuse, and notification flexibility. Only stores atomic email info, never cached tokens or codes. Example: primary and backup email tracking; supports search, notification, verification workflows.

Key relationships: Foreign key to discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: unique constraint on (discussionboard_member_id, email), optional verification per email.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique email record identifier.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Each email mapped to a registered user.
- `email`: Email address string associated with the account. Implements registration, notification, and recovery flows - separate from core username for flexibility. Ensures normalization. Example: jane@host.com.
- `is_verified`: Whether the email has passed verification (registration, notification, etc). Implements email confirmation flow; only verified addresses are used for key system functions. Defaults to false until confirmation.
- `is_primary`: Whether this email is the primary contact address for the member (UI and system requirement). Each account can have at most one primary email. For example: used for login, password reset.
- `added_at`: Datetime this email address was added or linked. Supports registration, change tracking, and reporting requirements.
- `verified_at`: Datetime when verification was completed. Nullable to allow in-progress or failed verifications. Maintains normalization; no denormalized workflow states.

### `discussionboard_user_auths`

External/federated authentication records - Implements secure multi-provider authentication flows per non-functional requirements (Authentication API & Security).

Normalizes all external auth connections (OAuth, SSO) for each account, supporting identity linking, revocation, and RBAC; stores only atomic data and references. Example: Google/Facebook/Twitter/SSO logins mapped to a user. Key relationships: Foreign key to discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: Composite uniqueness (member, provider, provider_user_id).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique external authentication record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - the member holding this external auth.
- `provider`: Authentication provider/service name (e.g., google, facebook, github). Implements SSO/federated auth requirement. Normalized string, never contains secrets. Example: 'google'.
- `provider_user_id`: User identifier from auth provider (not internal ID). Used for provider-based account merging and uniqueness/lookup. Example: OAuth subject ID.
- `linked_at`: Datetime this external auth connection was established. For sign-on/audit purposes; always required.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime external auth was revoked/unlinked (null if active). Implements revocation/idle account closure workflows.

### `discussionboard_user_sessions`

Active and historical login sessions for members - Implements authentication, auditing, session management, and inactivity/logout flows (see: Authentication & Security)

Each record represents one signed-in session for a member, using opaque tokens. Maintains security by avoiding caching sensitive credentials; stores only atomic values (tokens, validity timestamps), never pre-calculated or denormalized status. For example, used for login expiration, forced logout, device management.

Key relationships: Foreign key to discussionboard_members. Special behaviors: Tokens unique, support session trace/logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique session record identifier.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Referenced member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Each session is associated with a single member.
- `session_token`: Opaque authentication token for this session. Used client-side for identifying login state. Uniqueness enforced; never stores raw credentials. Example: random UUID or JWT value.
- `created_at`: Datetime session was created. Enables security/audit trace, expiry/refresh handling.
- `expires_at`: Datetime when the session token will expire. Supports session timeout and security policies. Example: set per login policy or on grant.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime session was revoked/invalidated (e.g., logout, idle timeout, forced admin action). Null if still valid. Maintains data integrity and audit trail.

### `discussionboard_posts`

Discussion Board Posts - This implements the core posting requirement from the requirements document (sections 2.2, 2.3). Represents top-level user posts within boards, tracking authorship, timestamps, and relation to board. Strict 3NF: all aggregate data (like counts, view counts) are handled in separate tables or materialized views. Links to edits, likes, views, comments. Example usage: a member or moderator creates a new discussion topic under a board.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `board_id`: Belonged board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards)
- `author_id`: Author user's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) (or moderator/admin).
- `title`: Title of the post. Atomic for search and filter.
- `body`: Full body/content of post. No derived or calculated fields.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Nullable soft-deletion timestamp if deleted by moderation.

### `discussionboard_post_edits`

Discussion Board Post Edit Log - Implements snapshot pattern for edit/audit trail compliance. Each row records an edit event for a post, including editor identity and timestamp. No aggregation. Used for edit history, moderation transparency (3NF).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Edited post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts)
- `editor_id`: User who made the edit, references member/mod/admin.
- `edit_summary`: Optional description of what changed.
- `edited_at`: Timestamp of edit event.

### `discussionboard_post_likes`

Discussion Board Post Likes/Dislikes - Each row is a user's like/dislike for a specific post (3NF-compliant; no aggregates). Used for engagement analytics, anti-abuse, audit trail. Unique per (post_id, user_id).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Liked/disliked post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts)
- `user_id`: Expressing user id (member/mod/admin) [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)
- `is_like`: True if like, false if dislike.
- `created_at`: Event timestamp.

### `discussionboard_post_views`

Discussion Board Post Views - Each row is a tracked viewing event, atomic and 3NF. No aggregated view counts stored. References viewer (nullable if anonymous/guest), post, and session. Example usage: user/visitor views a post; a row is logged for analytics and anti-abuse purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Viewed post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts)
- `user_id`: Viewer id (nullable for unauthenticated/guest view) [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)
- `session_id`: Session id for anonymous/guest view tracking; useful for analytics. Nullable.
- `viewed_at`: Timestamp view occurred.

### `discussionboard_comments`

Discussion Board Comments (Replies) - Implements comment/nested reply feature. Each row is an atomic comment (not aggregate or summary); threaded/reply-to is enabled via parent_id. Relates to a post, optional parent comment, and has author and timestamps. Example: a reply to a comment will set parent_id; a reply to post will keep parent_id null.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: The post this comment is on [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts)
- `author_id`: Comment author's user id (member/mod/admin) [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)
- `parent_id`: Optional recursive parent for a reply chain (refers to this table's id). Nullable for top-level replies.
- `body`: Comment text (atomic, not computed).
- `created_at`: Timestamp created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for moderation/audit purposes.

### `discussionboard_comment_likes`

Likes/Dislikes for Discussion Board Comments - 3NF: one row per user per comment liking or disliking. No aggregate or summary fields. Used for engagement analytics, anti-abuse. Unique per (comment_id, user_id).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `comment_id`: Liked/disliked comment id [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments)
- `user_id`: Reacting user id (member/mod/admin) [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)
- `is_like`: True if like, false if dislike.
- `created_at`: Timestamp like/dislike event was created.

### `discussionboard_comment_edits`

Discussion Board Comment Edit Log - Each row is an atomic edit event for a comment (snapshot audit pattern). Tracks which comment was edited, who did it, and when. Used for audit transparency in moderation context (3NF).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `comment_id`: Edited comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments)
- `editor_id`: User who edited the comment [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)
- `edit_summary`: Optional brief note on edit reason or summary.
- `edited_at`: Edit event timestamp.

### `discussionboard_comment_views`

Unique view/read tracking for comments (analytics, engagement). Atomic: one row per (comment, user/session); no aggregates. Relates to comment, viewing user (nullable/guest), and session. Used for analytics/reporting (never pre-calculated).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `comment_id`: Viewed comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments)
- `user_id`: User id of viewer (nullable/guest) [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members)
- `session_id`: Nullable session id to support anonymous/guest visitor analytics.
- `viewed_at`: Timestamp of view event.

### `discussionboard_reports`

User-generated content reports - This implements requirements from 'Moderation & Community Guidelines' and 'Functional Requirements: Flag/Report Functionality'. 
Allows members to report inappropriate posts or comments for moderator/admin review. Maintains 3NF compliance by storing one report per row with foreign keys linking to reporting member and target content. For example, when a member reports a comment, a record is created with details about the report and the referenced comment. 
Key relationships: References reporter (discussionboard_members), content type (post/comment), and target content.
Special behaviors: Only one active report per content per reporting member is allowed until resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each report.
- `reporting_member_id`: Referencing the member who filed the report: [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `target_post_id`: Referenced post if report concerns a post: [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts). Nullable if report is for a comment.
- `target_comment_id`: Referenced comment if report concerns a comment: [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments). Nullable if report is for a post.
- `reason`
  > Reason for reporting - Implements the 'report reason' requirement.
  > Describes why the member has flagged the content. Ensures normalization by storing descriptive report reasons. For example, 'hate speech', 'spam', 'off-topic'.
- `status`: Status of the report (e.g., pending, reviewed, resolved, rejected). Implements 'moderation workflow' requirements. Only controlled values allowed through app logic.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the report was filed. Supports moderation audit trails and reporting flow. Always required.
- `reviewed_at`: Timestamp of when moderators reviewed the report. Nullable until review occurs.
- `resolved_at`: Timestamp when action was taken or report was closed. Nullable until resolved.
- `moderation_note`: Moderator/admin remarks/comments for this report. Implements 'reviewer comment' requirement. Nullable if moderators did not leave notes.

### `discussionboard_moderation_actions`

Moderator or admin actions taken during moderation - Implements the 'Moderation Dashboards' and 'Action Audit Trail' requirements.
Tracks all key actions performed by moderators/admins (e.g., content removal, warning issued, ban applied). Maintains 3NF compliance by recording one action per row linked to the actor and the relevant report/content. For example, when a moderator removes a violating post, the action is logged with actor ID, action type, timestamp, and optional notes.
Key relationships: Links to actor (admin/moderator/member), the related report, and optionally, the target post or comment. Supports auditability and moderation transparency.
Special behaviors: Serialized log for moderation actions for full traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for moderation action record.
- `actor_admin_id`: Actor if admin performed the action: [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Nullable if actor is moderator/member.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Actor if moderator performed the action: [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Nullable if actor is admin/member.
- `actor_member_id`: Actor if member performed the action: [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Nullable if actor is admin/moderator. For transparency, in case members can self-resolve or retract reports.
- `related_report_id`: Linked report this action addresses: [discussionboard_reports.id](#discussionboard_reports). Nullable if not directly linked.
- `target_post_id`: Target post acted upon (if applicable): [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `target_comment_id`: Target comment acted upon (if applicable): [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments).
- `action_type`
  > Type of moderation action (e.g. warn, ban, content removal, close report).
  > Implements moderation workflow requirements. Only controlled values allowed.
- `action_reason`: Details or reason for the moderation action. Implements 'audit and rationale' requirements. Example: 'Repeated violations', 'Spam content'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the moderation action was performed. Supports audit trails and workflow sequencing. Required for every action.

### `discussionboard_bans`

User bans from the platform - Implements business requirements in 'Moderation & Community Guidelines' and 'User Management'.
Represents temporary or permanent user bans imposed by admins or moderators. Maintains 3NF compliance with a table per ban event, linking to the banned user (admin, moderator, or member) and the actor imposing the ban. For example, when a moderator bans a user for policy violation, the record logs the target user, actor, period, reason, and status.
Key relationships: References the banned user (any role) and the actor.
Special behaviors: Only one active ban at a time per user. Ban status updates tracked by action logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for ban record.
- `target_admin_id`: Target if banned user was an admin: [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Nullable if target is not an admin.
- `target_moderator_id`: Target if banned user was a moderator: [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Nullable if target is not moderator.
- `target_member_id`: Target if banned user was a member: [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Nullable if not member.
- `actor_admin_id`: Admin who imposed the ban: [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Nullable unless ban imposed by admin.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Moderator who imposed the ban: [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Nullable unless ban imposed by moderator.
- `ban_reason`: Reason for ban - Implements explicit rationale requirement. Describes why user was banned. Ensures normalization. E.g. 'Severe harassment', 'Repeated spam'.
- `ban_start_at`: When ban starts. Implements requirement for configurable ban durations. Prevents premature enforcement on the record.
- `ban_end_at`: When ban ends (nullable if permanent). Enforces temporal normalization. E.g. 30-day ban, permanent if null.
- `status`: Ban status (e.g. active, expired, lifted, scheduled). Controls enforcement by application logic. Implements status audit requirement.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of ban record creation. Supports timeline and reporting.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for last update to ban record. Audits changes, supports compliance requirements.

### `discussionboard_warnings`

Warnings issued to users for infractions - Implements requirements under 'User Management' and 'Moderation Dashboards'.
Represents warnings (as opposed to bans) issued by moderators/admins to users for lesser violations. Maintains 3NF normalization: Each warning is linked to the warned user and the actor. Useful for progressive discipline enforcement. For example, members with repeated warnings may escalate to a ban.
Key relationships: Links to the warned user (admin/mod/member) and the actor (admin/mod). 
Special behaviors: Track number and reason for warnings for each user; escalation rules handled externally by application logic.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for warning record.
- `target_admin_id`: Warned admin (rare): [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Nullable if not admin.
- `target_moderator_id`: Warned moderator (rare): [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Nullable if not moderator.
- `target_member_id`: Warned member: [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Nullable if not member.
- `actor_admin_id`: Admin issuing warning: [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Nullable unless admin issued.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Moderator issuing warning: [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Nullable unless moderator issued.
- `related_report_id`: Related report (if warning is result of a report): [discussionboard_reports.id](#discussionboard_reports). Nullable if warning is not report-triggered.
- `reason`: Reason for issuing warning - Implements rationale requirement. E.g. 'Minor profanity', 'Off-topic'. Required for context audit.
- `created_at`: When warning was issued. For audit and escalation flows. Required for every warning.

### `discussionboard_audit_logs`

Detailed audit logs for moderation events - Implements all audit and logging requirements outlined under 'Audit & Logging' and referenced throughout Moderation functional requirements. 
Stores granular logs about all moderation events, including state changes, permission elevation, and sensitive moderation actions. Maintains 3NF: All fields are atomic, and each log references the related action, actor, and event time. For example, when a moderator changes the status of a report, an audit log is added with actor ID, event type, event detail, and when it occurred.
Key relationships: Links to actor (admin/mod/member) and optionally to related moderation action or report.
Special behaviors: Immutable by application design - supports regulatory and policy audit needs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for audit log entry.
- `actor_admin_id`: Admin actor (if applicable): [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins). Null if not admin.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Moderator actor (if applicable): [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators). Null if not moderator.
- `actor_member_id`: Member actor (if applicable): [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Null if not member.
- `related_report_id`: Related report (if log is for a report event): [discussionboard_reports.id](#discussionboard_reports). Nullable if not report-related.
- `related_moderation_action_id`: Related moderation action (if log is for an action event): [discussionboard_moderation_actions.id](#discussionboard_moderation_actions). Nullable if not related to an action.
- `event_type`: Type of event (e.g., permission_change, status_update, ban_imposed). Controlled by business logic for audit classification. Only allowed values accepted.
- `event_detail`: Detail about the event - Implements requirement for detailed traceability. Example: 'Report status changed from pending to resolved by moderator.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp for the logged event. For compliance and sequencing. Required on every audit entry.

### `discussionboard_community_guidelines`

Community Guidelines entity - This implements the clear community rule and code-of-conduct requirements as detailed in the Discussion Board Requirements section 1 (Community Rules & 01 Business Objectives). 

Business explanation: Stores guideline sections and texts in a normalized form, allowing updates and auditability for evolving community standards. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating each guideline entry, allowing references in moderation and user notifications. For example, guidelines about hate speech, constructive criticism, and post etiquette are stored here, referenced for automated onboarding or user display.

Key relationships: May be referenced by moderation or notification components for contextual messaging. Special behaviors: Only admins can create or update guidelines; each entry is versioned by created_at/updated_at for audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this guideline entry.
- `title`: Title of the guideline section - Implements requirement for clear, organized guideline presentation to users. For example, 'Posting Etiquette' or 'Prohibited Conduct.' Ensures normalization by storing as an atomic value.
- `body`: Full content text of the guideline - Implements detailed community rule requirements. For example, 'Do not post personal attacks or hate speech.' Normalized 3NF, no derived/consolidated data.
- `order_index`: Display order for this guideline - Required for user experience sequencing in guideline displays. Ensures atomicity and flexibility, supports updates without data duplication.
- `is_active`: Whether this guideline is currently enforced - Implements admin control of active/inactive statuses for evolving policy. For example, deactivating outdated rules. Ensures compliance with requirement to support updates and changes.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when guideline was created - Supports audit logging (requirement 2.6), and helps track policy evolution over time. Atomic value, part of full normalization.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when guideline was last updated. Ensures full auditability of content changes. 3NF compliance.

### `discussionboard_content_policies`

Content Policy entity - Implements the explicit, system-level policy and moderation documentation requirements as detailed in requirements section 3 (Content Policies & Moderation Policy).

Business purpose: Stores specific, enforceable policy rules that apply to user-generated content (e.g. 'No hate speech', 'No plagiarism'). Maintains normalization by handling each policy as a distinct, queryable record. Can be referenced during automated content checking or manual moderation. For example, policy text on 'Profanity' or 'Spam' detection is kept here.

Key relationships: May be referenced when determining sanction actions. Special behaviors: Only admins can add/update/delete policy entries. Supports audit trail with timestamps.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this content policy rule.
- `policy_code`: Short code or name for this content policy - Implements requirement for structured policy documentation and reference. Enables quick lookup and enforcement. For example, 'NO_HATE_SPEECH', 'NO_SPAM'.
- `description`: Detailed description of the content policy - Implements policy communication and moderator clarity requirements. For example, 'Any content promoting violence is strictly prohibited.' 3NF.
- `category`: Category or policy group - Implements requirement to organize content policies by type, e.g., 'Spam', 'Abuse', 'Copyright'. Ensures normalization by avoiding transitive dependencies.
- `is_active`: Whether this policy is active/enforced - Needed for content policy versioning and update flows. For example, deactivating obsolete policies. Ensures atomicity.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this policy was created. Required for audit trails and rollback scenarios (requirements 2.6, 4).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this policy was last updated - Ensures full auditability and supports policy review schedules.

### `discussionboard_profanity_filters`

Profanity Filter entity - Implements the system-level requirement for profanity filtering as outlined in requirements section 3.4 (Content Policies, Moderation).

Business purpose: Contains normalized words/phrases that trigger system profanity detection on posts and comments. Maintains 3NF by storing each profane word or phrase as a single record, linked to activation status and audit fields. For example, the word 'foobar' or a list of banned words.

Key relationships: May be referenced by automated moderation or content creation APIs. Special behaviors: Admins update/add words as needed, all events are timestamped.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique ID for this profanity filter entry.
- `word`: Word or phrase to be filtered - Implements requirement for configurable, updatable profanity filtering. Ensures normalized storage. For example, 'badword'.
- `is_active`: Whether this word is currently being filtered - Required for admin update flexibility. For example, suspending words from filter lists. Atomic value.
- `created_at`: When this filter entry was created - For auditability and policy management. 3NF value.
- `updated_at`: When this filter entry was last updated - Needed for rollbacks or removals in system logs, part of full normalization.

### `discussionboard_automated_spam_rules`

Automated Spam Rule entity - Implements the automated spam rule detection policies required by Functional Requirements 3.3.4 and Moderation Policy.

Business purpose: Stores configurable, versioned rules or patterns that the platform's automated spam detector references. Maintains 3NF by separating each spam rule (regex, expression, or keyword) as an atomic record. For example, an entry could define regex matching repeated links or banned spam phrases.

Key relationships: May be consumed by content creation or moderation APIs. Special behaviors: Rule activation handled by admins, all updates tracked in audit logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this spam rule entry.
- `rule_pattern`: Pattern or expression for spam detection - Implements flexible, updatable automated spam pattern detection. 3NF compliance. For example, regex for repeated links or specific spam syntax.
- `description`: Explanation of what this rule detects - Implements clarity and auditability. For example, 'Detects repeated posting of phishing URLs.' Atomic, not derived.
- `is_active`: Whether the rule is currently active - Allows admins to enable/disable detection flexibly for evolving spam tactics. Ensures policy agility.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this spam rule was created - Required for audit logging and rule review processes.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this spam rule was last updated - Ensures full auditability of rule changes. 3NF compliance.

### `discussionboard_notifications`

Discussion Board Notification Entity - Implements the notification delivery requirement from the Notification System and Audit & Logging sections. 

This model stores each notification event (such as replies, likes, mentions, moderation actions) sent to users. It allows tracking, delivery status, and historic audit for every notification generated by system events across the discussion board.

Maintains 3NF compliance by separating notification records from user profiles and alert preferences (notification delivery configuration is stored in a separate table). For example, when a user receives a reply to their post, a notification record is created here, referencing the recipient, event details, and delivery state.

Key relationships: Links to recipients (discussionboard_members) via foreign key. Optionally relates to specific posts, comments, or moderation events stored in other domains.
Special behaviors: Notifications can be marked as read/unread. Supports expirable and persistent notification types.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each notification.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Recipient's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - The user who receives this notification. Fulfills the requirement for per-user notification tracking and targeting.
- `type`: Notification type - Implements the Notification System requirement specifying kind of event (e.g., 'reply', 'like', 'mention', 'moderation_action', 'system'). Defines the user event that triggered notification delivery. Ensures normalization by recording type as a code, not a computed string. Example: 'reply'.
- `related_entity_id`: Reference ID of the related entity (e.g., post, comment, moderation action) - Implements the Notification System's requirement for contextual notification. Stores the target object relevant to the notification for audit/logging. Can be null if event is generic. Ensures normalization by storing only the ID. Example: the comment being replied to.
- `related_entity_type`: Type of related entity referenced (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'moderation_action') - Implements requirement to allow notifications on multiple kinds of entities. Ensures normalization by specifying entity type in a discrete field, not by using polymorphic joins. Example: 'post'.
- `content`: Notification message content - Implements requirement for human-readable notification body. Stores the message shown to the user. Example: 'Alice replied to your post.' Field is atomic and normalized. No computed values here.
- `is_read`: Flag indicating whether the notification has been read. Supports UI requirements for marking notifications as read/unread. Ensures normalization by only storing a boolean flag. Example: false (unread).
- `delivered_at`: Timestamp when notification was delivered to the user. Implements audit/logging requirements for notification delivery history and sequencing. Normalization: Each delivery occurrence is atomic. Example: 2024-06-17T12:00:00Z.
- `expires_at`: Timestamp when notification expires - Implements event-driven notification expiry (for temporary/scheduled alerts). Ensures normalization by storing expiry per notification, not per user. Example: 2024-07-01T00:00:00Z. May be null if notification does not expire.

### `discussionboard_alert_preferences`

Discussion Board Alert Preference Entity - Implements the notification preferences requirement from the Notification System and Settings functionality sections. 

This model stores each user's per-type notification delivery preferences (e.g., email, push, in-app, or off). Fulfills the requirement to provide members with fine-grained control over which notification types they receive and how they are delivered.

Maintains 3NF compliance by separating user notification configuration from actual notification data and user profile records. For example, a user may choose in-app alerts for replies but email notifications for moderation actions, which is configured here.

Key relationships: References the user (discussionboard_members) as the owner of these preferences. No denormalized or computed fields.
Special behaviors: Only one set of preferences per (user, notification type) enforced by unique index constraint.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each alert preference record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Owner's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - The user who owns this alert preference set. Implements per-user preference requirement for notification delivery.
- `notification_type`: Notification type for which this preference applies (e.g., 'reply', 'like', 'mention', 'moderation_action', 'system') - Implements the Notification System and Settings requirements for configurable per-type delivery. Ensures normalization by storing type as atomic value. Example: 'moderation_action'.
- `delivery_channel`: Delivery channel preference (e.g., 'email', 'push', 'in_app', 'none') - Implements requirement for per-type delivery method configuration by user. Ensures normalization by storing as atomic value, not as calculated field. Example: 'email'.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when these preferences were last updated. Supports audit/logging for settings changes. Ensures atomic history of preference changes. Example: 2024-06-18T13:31:21Z.

### `discussionboard_action_logs`

[Discussion Board Action Logs] - This implements the audit trail, accountability, and compliance requirements from the requirements document (including 2.6 Audit & Logging, moderation, and transparency mandates).

Records every critical user or system action, especially for admin/moderator-level events. Maintains 3NF (fully normalized) by separating actor ID, event types, and contextual entity references, supports extensible metadata, and avoids denormalization. Example: logs a moderator deleting a post or editing a comment.

Key relationships: Connects to user tables such as [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins), [discussionboard_moderators.id](#discussionboard_moderators), or other actors by "actor_id" field.
Special behaviors: Immutable log entries, supports efficient filtering by actor/event/time; forms basis for compliance reporting and root-cause investigation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each log entry.
- `actor_id`: Actor's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members), [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins), or related user type associated with this action. This ties each log entry to the user responsible for the action, supporting auditability and cross-user queries.
- `event_type`: Type of action performed. Implements event categorization (e.g., POST_CREATED, COMMENT_DELETED, MODERATOR_BAN). Enables filtering and auditing by action nature. Ensures normalization by not encoding rules in single fields. Example: 'POST_DELETED'.
- `event_target_id`: Associated entity ID for this action (e.g., post, comment, report), implements requirement for contextual event reference. Maintains normalized design by storing IDs only. Example: The comment or post UUID affected. Nullable if event affects no entity.
- `metadata`: Additional JSON metadata for extensibility (e.g., IP address, device, moderation reason). Implements extensibility and normalization by not hardcoding new columns for rare event data. Example: '{"reason":"Spam","ip":"10.1.2.3"}'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the action occurred. Implements mandatory audit resolution and helps support sorting/filtering by time. Example: '2025-07-22T13:30:45.969+09:00'.

### `discussionboard_error_logs`

[Error Logging Table] - This implements requirements from 3.1 Security, 3.2 Performance, and 3.5 Compliance regarding platform and API error capture for diagnostics and resilience.

Captures and audits all system or application errors and exceptions in a normalized, traceable log. 3NF compliance by completely separating error details from business records, with reference context available via "context_id". Used in debugging, incident response, or platform monitoring. Example: logs database faults, uncaught exceptions, and failed external API calls.

Key relationships: No direct foreign keys (for privacy and decoupling from actor data).
Special behaviors: Immutable, full-text searchable, supports quick triage by error code and time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `error_code`: Application-defined error or exception code. Enables quick error categorization and system monitoring. Example: 'API_TIMEOUT', 'UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION'.
- `error_message`: Human-readable error message for reporting and debugging. Meets compliance for log clarity. Example: 'Failed to fetch posts due to network timeout.'
- `stack_trace`: Full stack trace or technical details for debugging. Fulfills non-functional requirements for detailed auditing; normalized by isolating trace info from other data. Nullable if unavailable. Example: JavaScript stack trace or error object.
- `context_id`: Arbitrary context entity (e.g., API request ID or related entity UUID). Supports linking errors to request or entity. Nullable if not applicable.
- `created_at`: Timestamp the error was recorded, allows sequencing and SLA tracking. Example: '2025-07-22T13:30:45.969+09:00'.

### `discussionboard_api_access_logs`

[API Access Logs] - Implements non-functional requirements 3.1 Security, 3.2 Performance, and 2.6 Audit by tracing all API interactions for security review, rate-limiting enforcement, and usage analytics.

Logs all API calls, including the user (if authenticated), endpoint, HTTP method, and result. Maintains normalization (3NF) with user linkage by actor_id (nullable for guests), never storing denormalized request payloads. Used for monitoring abuse and generating analytics. Example: logs a member's GET to /api/posts or a failed POST to /api/comments.

Key relationships: May reference the user by actor_id (nullable for guest requests). No other foreign keys.
Special behaviors: Massive write-optimized; may be purged for data retention compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `actor_id`: Authenticated user's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members), [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins), or related role. Null if guest/public API. Enables audit and correlation to users.
- `method`: HTTP method used for this API call (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, etc). Implements API audit detail. Example: 'GET'.
- `endpoint`: API endpoint path or resource accessed. Enables fine-grained analytics. Example: '/api/comments/12345'.
- `status_code`: Returned HTTP status code. Allows compliance and diagnostics on failed/successful calls. Example: 200, 403, 404.
- `ip_address`: IP address of the client for this call. Supports abuse monitoring and incident forensics. Example: '203.0.113.5'.
- `user_agent`: Client user-agent for context in debugging or device profiling. Nullable if unavailable. Example: 'Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 14_2 like Mac OS X)'.
- `response_time_ms`: Request processing latency in milliseconds. Enables API performance monitoring. Example: 163.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of the API call. Supports retention and incident analysis. Example: '2025-07-22T13:30:45.969+09:00'.

operations.specification: Implements retrieval of a paginated or filtered list of board sections for the political/economic discussion board. This operation fetches all sections (such as 'Politics', 'Economy') which are used for organizing sets of boards. Follows list/read/search pattern and supports possible query, pagination, or filter data to be supplied in request body. Based on table: discussionboard_sections.
operations.description:
This API provides a way to retrieve a filtered and/or paginated list of discussion board sections. Each section organizes boards under broad themes (e.g., politics, economy). Only atomic data from the discussionboard_sections table is returned: section id, name, description, sort_order, created_at, updated_at. operations.specification: Create a new audit log entry for significant events related to moderation, access, or system actions in the Discussion Board platform. This endpoint is primarily used to store immutable audit records for actions taken by admins, moderators, or system processes. It references the 'discussionboard_audit_logs' table, which records who performed the action, event type, detail, and contextual entity references per requirement 2.6 in moderation and compliance mandates. Only allowed for system/integration/admin operations - regular members are not permitted to arbitrarily create logs. Data must be immutable after creation (except for structured compliance adjustments) to support regulatory and incident root-cause analysis.
operations.description:
This API operation creates a new entry in the 'discussionboard_audit_logs' table to record a system-level, moderation, or user action. Each record contains information about the actor (admin, moderator, member), the nature of the event (such as permission elevation, report status update, ban imposition), optional references to related moderation/report actions, and a detailed log of what transpired. Actions recorded include but are not limited to: moderator actions on reports, warnings, bans, permission changes, and audit-relevant configuration changes. 

The audit log maintains strict 3NF normalization: all fields are atomic and must reference existing entities by foreign key where needed. Log entries are immutable, created at the moment of the event for traceability. Only platform/internal logic or admin users with explicit permission should access this endpoint.

Returned values include the new audit log entry as persisted in the DB. Error states include invalid/unauthorized creation attempts, missing references, or DB constraints violations.
